FOMC01.case: summer statement, 'For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT'

FOMC02.case: winter statement, 'For release at 2:00 p.m. EST'

FOMC03.verdict: VALID event; declared_release_at = null; content source_available_at = null; NOT parser failure

FOMC04.verdict: no timezone guess; declared_release_at = null; content source_available_at = null

FOMC05.case: feed shows item, primary page unavailable
FOMC05.verdict: NO EventRevision; SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; discovery raw retained; retried on a later normal poll; observed_at NEVER taken from discovery

FOMC06.case: primary page observed 90s after declared release
FOMC06.verdict: declared_release_at = release instant (metadata only); observed_at = +90s; source_available_at = null; durable visibility from max(observed_at, ingested_at)

FOMC08.verdict: append a NEW immutable revision; GUID is never proof of unchanged content

FOMC09.case: different GUID unexpectedly maps to the same logical item
FOMC09.verdict: FAIL CLOSED identity conflict; no 'latest wins'

FOMC10.verdict: Last Update is not source_available_at, not source_updated_at, not vintage proof, not revision chronology, not an identity input; declared_release_at unchanged

FOMC11.verdict: declared_release_at MAY record the trusted 2026 release metadata. observed_at = the actual 2027 fetch; ingested_at = the 2027 commit; content source_available_at = null. DURABLE_OBSERVED before 2027: ABSENT. RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE MUST NOT expose the 2027-fetched body as content visible in 2026 - no vintage proof.

FOMC12.verdict: verified replay FAILS CLOSED; no network repair

FOMC15.case: valid feed, zero new FOMC items
FOMC15.verdict: EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO only when ALL seven preconditions hold - in particular complete deterministic classification and zero unresolved candidates - and the assertion is scoped to the V1 capture subset

FOMC16.case: normalization transaction fails after raw persisted
FOMC16.verdict: no ingested_at, no EventRevision visibility; raw survives for rebuild

FOMC17.verdict: the committed revision remains authoritative and is rediscovered idempotently

FOMC18.verdict: no new content revision; observation metadata still auditable

FOMC19.case: HISTORICAL CORRECTED BODY - 14:00 original release H1; 16:00 upstream correction to H2; 2026 first HyprL backfill retrieves H2; the page still prints the original 14:00 release line
FOMC19.verdict: declared_release_at = 14:00 (event metadata). H2: source_available_at = null, observed_at = the 2026 fetch, ingested_at = the 2026 commit. RETROSPECTIVE_SOURCE at 14:30: H2 NOT VISIBLE. No claim is made that H1 was available either - H1 was never captured and its vintage was never proven.

FOMC20.case: LIVE CORRECTION RETAINING THE ORIGINAL RELEASE LINE - 14:00 release; 14:00:30 H1 captured; 16:00 recheck captures H2; both bodies print "For release at 2:00"
FOMC20.verdict: H1 visibility bounded by its own observed_at/ingested_at; H2 visibility bounded by its own. NEITHER revision inherits 14:00 as source_available_at. declared_release_at = 14:00 is event metadata only.

FOMC21.case: FIRST LIVE FETCH AFTER DECLARED RELEASE - declared 14:00:00, first primary receipt 14:00:47
FOMC21.verdict: even the INITIAL body cannot be proven byte-for-byte to have existed at 14:00:00, so content source_available_at = null and durable visibility begins from observed/commit. This closes a subtle 47-second retroprojection.

FOMC22.case: UNSCHEDULED MONETARY ACTION WITH A DIFFERENT TITLE - feed fetch and parse succeed; an official item is plausibly monetary/FOMC but its title differs from the frozen predicate
FOMC22.verdict: NOT normalized under V1. classification = UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE. EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO is PROHIBITED for that cycle. No claim is made that the event did not exist. Raw feed evidence retained. A future CaptureSpec may add the family.

FOMC23.case: FEED TITLE MATCHES, PRIMARY PAGE TITLE DIFFERS
FOMC23.verdict: discovery/primary classification CONFLICT. No normalized event, no zero assertion, and NO silent downgrade to DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE. Diagnostic and raw provenance retained; PARSER_FAILED for that surface.

FOMC24.case: SUCCESSFUL CYCLE WITH ZERO MATCHES AND ZERO UNRESOLVED CANDIDATES - feed raw persisted, parse succeeds, every relevant entry deterministically outside the V1 subset, no pending or failing candidate
FOMC24.verdict: EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO PERMITTED, and explicitly scoped to the V1 capture subset - not to all FOMC monetary-policy activity.

FOMC25.case: POSITIVE FEED CANDIDATE, PRIMARY FETCH FAILS
FOMC25.verdict: no normalized event; candidate remains unresolved; SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on the primary surface; EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO PROHIBITED. "0 normalized events" is not zero.

FOMC26.case: OFFICIAL DATE CORRECTION ON SAME URL - R3/X6
FOMC26.preconditions: same P, E and U; H1 != H2; D1 != D2; both observations satisfy the existing normalization requirements
FOMC26.same_body_control: identical verified primary body bytes under the SAME CaptureSpec hash MUST yield the same official_statement_date. A different date is a PARSER/NORMALIZER DETERMINISM FAILURE: FAIL CLOSED, no new content revision, no normalized overwrite.
FOMC26.verdict: SAME source_item_id S; append R2 with D2; retain R1 with D1 unchanged. Date correction alone is NOT an identity conflict. No duplicate logical event, no overwrite, no retroactive visibility mutation. Both revisions retain source_available_at = null and source_updated_at = null, with their own observed_at and ingested_at.
FOMC26.with_guid: same GUID on both observations: SAME S, R2 appended; existing GUID conflicts still fail closed if independently triggered
FOMC26.without_guid: historical archive/backfill, no RSS GUID on either observation: SAME S, R2 appended; GUID absence does not alter identity

FOMC27.preconditions: U1 is extracted from a durable official feed/archive artifact and passes existing validation; U1 -> U2 satisfies existing redirect security rules
FOMC27.verdict: canonical_primary_statement_url = normalize(U1) using existing url_canonicalization; source_item_id derives from that value. U2 and the redirect chain are transport provenance only. NEVER re-key from normalize(U2). Computing identity does not bypass existing primary classification or revision-admission requirements.

FOMC28.preconditions: same provider_id and event_family; same normalized official discovery URL; both redirect chains pass existing security rules
FOMC28.same_body: SAME content revision; transport movement alone creates no content revision
FOMC28.changed_body: append a NEW immutable content revision under SAME S according to existing revision_policy
FOMC28.verdict: U1 -> U2 then U1 -> U3 keeps canonical_primary_statement_url = normalize(U1) and source_item_id = S. Record differing transport provenance. No new logical item and no identity conflict solely from the redirect-topology change; existing independent GUID conflicts still apply.

FOMC29.verdict: a primary-page <link rel="canonical" href="U4"> has NO semantic or identity authority in V1. Identity remains normalize(U1); no replacement, merge, split, re-key or identity conflict solely because U4 differs. If retained, U4 is optional non-authoritative diagnostic/provenance only.

FOMC30.verdict: U1 comes from a durable official calendar/archive statement link, passes existing validation and normalization, and anchors source_item_id before U1 -> U2. No GUID required; no identity from U2, HTML canonical or a synthetic date-derived URL. Existing backfill visibility and admission requirements remain unchanged.

FOMC31.preconditions: same provider_id and event_family; only the ASCII scheme casing differs; existing official-discovery and non-scheme URL validation requirements hold
FOMC31.verdict: ACCEPT HTTPS scheme using ASCII case-insensitive comparison; serialize exactly lowercase ASCII https in canonical_primary_statement_url. Every listed scheme spelling yields expected_identity_url and the SAME source_item_id. Original spelling remains in durable raw discovery provenance only. Scheme case alone causes no new source item, identity conflict or content revision; all existing primary admission requirements still apply.

FOMC32.verdict: REJECT at scheme admission. NEVER silently upgrade http to https. No canonical identity URL, no source_item_id admission and no primary request. ftp, file, data, javascript and an empty/missing scheme are also rejected under scheme_admission.

canonical_serialization.generated_at_field: deliberately absent so the spec hash is reproducible
canonical_serialization.rule: json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8'), SHA-256 over those bytes

future_fixture_requirements.capture_authorization: real historical raw fixtures may be captured only after implementation is authorised
required_before_implementation_is_accept: a summer EDT statement
a winter EST statement
a historical 'For immediate release' statement
an unchanged re-fetch
a synthetic changed-content revision
a synthetic malformed release line
a feed item whose primary fetch initially fails
a historical corrected body backfilled later (FOMC19)
a live correction retaining the original release line (FOMC20)
a first live fetch strictly after the declared release instant (FOMC21)
an unscheduled monetary item with a differing title (FOMC22)
a feed/primary title conflict (FOMC23)
a clean zero cycle with no unresolved candidates (FOMC24)
same canonical primary URL with date D1/H1 corrected to D2/H2 and the same RSS GUID: same logical item, appended revision (FOMC26)
historical archive/backfill with the same canonical primary URL and NO RSS GUID, date D1/H1 corrected to D2/H2: same logical item, appended revision (FOMC26 / R3-X6)
identical verified primary body bytes and the same CaptureSpec hash with conflicting parsed dates: fail closed, no new content revision (FOMC26 same-body control)
official discovery link U1 redirecting to U2: identity from normalized U1 (FOMC27)
same discovery U1 redirecting first to U2, later to U3: stable logical identity, with both unchanged-body and changed-body controls (FOMC28)
primary HTML canonical U4 differing from discovery U1: no identity authority (FOMC29)
historical official archive link U1 redirecting to U2 without an RSS GUID: identity from normalized U1 (FOMC30)
HTTPS, Https, hTtPs, HtTpS and https scheme spellings converge to the exact lowercase-https identity URL and source_item_id (FOMC31)
http and other non-HTTPS or empty/missing schemes are rejected without upgrade, source_item_id admission or primary request (FOMC32)
future_fixture_requirements.status: REQUIREMENTS ONLY - no fixture captured, no network in this phase

http_policy.conditional_requests: V1 CORRECTNESS MUST NOT DEPEND ON HTTP 304. A conditional request may never be the reason a raw artefact is missing. Any later use requires separate review.
http_policy.max_redirects_note: tightens urllib's default of 10; must be enforced explicitly
http_policy.redirect_rule: validated BEFORE being followed; destination must stay on the allowlist; off-allowlist => fail closed, host never contacted
http_policy.user_agent_note: repo convention hyprl-trading-lab-<purpose>/<version>. No personal e-mail, no secret, no browser impersonation.

identity.aliasing_non_goal_v1: NO automatic alias equivalence or global deduplication across distinct normalized official discovery URLs is claimed. Different normalized identity URLs remain distinct logical source items unless an already-frozen conflict rule independently blocks admission. Do not merge using body hash, date, title, HTML canonical or final redirect destination; alias equivalence requires a separately frozen policy.
identity.canonical_primary_statement_url: normalize(official_discovery_link_before_redirect), where normalize is EXACTLY the existing url_canonicalization policy. The word canonical means the normalized official discovery-link URL selected by this identity policy; it does not mean the final response URL or a remote HTML canonical URL.
identity.canonical_url_boundary: FIX4 freezes WHICH INPUT enters existing URL normalization: the official discovery link BEFORE primary network redirects. URL normalization transforms and redirect security rules are unchanged. General alias resolution is not introduced. FIX3 date-correction stability remains intact.

conflict_policy.resolution: never 'latest wins'; persist conflict diagnostics and raw provenance; no trusted normalized event until a deterministic resolution policy admits it

date_correction.downstream_dedupe: D1 and corrected D2 are revision metadata of the SAME source_item_id; downstream MUST NOT count them as two independent logical FOMC events merely because the date changed
date_correction.existing_guid_conflicts: preserved unchanged; apply conflict_policy if independently triggered. A date correction by itself is NOT an identity conflict, and is never a reason to split the item.
date_correction.revision_metadata: official_statement_date belongs to the observed content revision. If H1/D1 becomes H2/D2 with a changed body hash, append a NEW immutable content revision under the SAME source_item_id. Retain H1/D1 intact; no overwrite. Identical-body discrepancies follow parser_policy.official_statement_date_determinism.
date_correction.rule: same provider_id + same event_family + same canonical_primary_statement_url => SAME logical source item, regardless of an official_statement_date correction
date_correction.visibility: each revision keeps source_available_at = null and source_updated_at = null, and its own actual observed_at and commit-bound ingested_at. Identity repair never rewrites observed_at, ingested_at or declared_release_at on an existing revision. D2 is metadata, not source_updated_at, correction timing or content-vintage evidence; no retroactive availability change.
date_correction.with_guid: same canonical primary URL and same RSS GUID with D1 -> D2: SAME source_item_id; append a revision if the body hash changes
date_correction.without_guid: same canonical primary URL in historical archive/backfill with no RSS GUID and D1 -> D2: SAME source_item_id; append a revision if the body hash changes. GUID absence does not alter logical identity.

identity.discovery_link_mutation: a change in the official discovery link from U1 to a differently normalized U2 is NOT a redirect-topology change. The existing item keeps its stored U1-derived identity. A newly discovered U2 follows existing conflict/dedupe semantics only; no alias inference, identity rewrite or 'latest URL wins'.
identity.final_response_url_role: NON-IDENTIFYING TRANSPORT PROVENANCE: final allowlisted response URL after redirects. It MUST NOT replace canonical_primary_statement_url or re-key an item, including when it differs from discovery or changes on a later observation. Existing security validation still applies.
identity.guid_note: historical statements may lie outside current feed depth; identity must not depend on the feed
identity.historical_discovery_url_role: the statement link extracted from the durable official Federal Reserve calendar/archive artifact supplies the pre-redirect identity input, under the same validation and normalization as LIVE. No synthesized URL from date; no RSS GUID required; no identity from final response or HTML canonical.
identity.html_canonical_role: NON-IDENTIFYING, NON-AUTHORITATIVE: <link rel="canonical"> is ignored for V1 semantics and logical identity. It MUST NOT replace canonical_primary_statement_url, change source_item_id, merge or split items, or override official discovery identity. A mismatch alone is NOT an identity conflict. If retained at all, it is optional diagnostic/provenance only; no network retrieval is authorized by this field.
identity.identity_url_input_stage: official statement link parsed from the already DURABLE official discovery artifact, BEFORE the primary HTTP request and BEFORE following any primary redirect
identity_url_order: 1. fetch and durably persist the official discovery artifact under existing raw-first/provenance rules
2. parse its official statement link U_discovered
3. validate U_discovered using existing V1 URL/security rules
4. apply the EXISTING frozen url_canonicalization policy to U_discovered
5. bind the resulting value as canonical_primary_statement_url
6. compute source_item_id from provider_id, event_family and that value using existing canonical_serialization
7. perform the primary HTTP request for the discovered statement under existing HTTP policy
9. persist the redirect chain and U_final as transport provenance under existing raw policy
identity.identity_url_precomputation: computing a candidate identity before the primary fetch does NOT admit an EventRevision or an IN_SCOPE_V1 event; existing primary classification, raw-first, normalization and commit-bound visibility requirements remain mandatory
identity.live_discovery_url_role: the official monetary-policy RSS item's <link> extracted from its durable feed artifact supplies the pre-redirect identity input. Validate it, apply existing normalization and derive source_item_id before primary redirects. RSS GUID remains discovery provenance/consistency signal only.
identity.missing_canonical_url: FAIL CLOSED under the existing identity policy if a stable canonical primary URL cannot be established. No date fallback, no (provider_id, event_family, date) fallback and no GUID+date fallback may manufacture a logical identity.

provenance_url_roles.discovered_url: official statement link extracted from the durable discovery artifact; only its existing-policy normalized value supplies the logical URL identity
provenance_url_roles.final_response_url: final allowlisted URL after primary redirects, corresponding to existing raw policy's final URL provenance
provenance_url_roles.redirect_chain: ordered transport provenance of the primary request hops
provenance_url_roles.request_url: URL actually requested at a given hop; transport provenance, not a replacement identity input after derivation
provenance_url_roles.storage_note: semantic roles within existing raw/observation provenance, not a new raw or normalized schema; keep discovery provenance distinct from request, redirect and final response provenance

identity.redirect_identity_role: NON-IDENTIFYING TRANSPORT PROVENANCE: redirect destinations and the ordered redirect chain MUST NOT replace the discovered identity URL, merge or split items, or re-key source_item_id. Redirect differences alone are NOT identity conflicts; existing independent GUID conflicts remain unchanged.
identity.redirect_topology_change_behavior: for the same provider_id, event_family and normalized official discovery URL, U1 -> U2 then U1 -> U3 yields the SAME canonical_primary_statement_url = normalize(U1) and the SAME source_item_id. Transport movement alone creates neither a logical item nor a content revision: identical body follows same_item_same_body_hash; changed body follows same_item_different_body_hash under that same item.
identity.reobservation_identity_stability: scheduled re-observations retain the stored canonical_primary_statement_url derived from original discovery U1. A request may start from that official identity URL; the final destination observed that day MUST NOT recompute or rewrite item identity. No scheduler, recheck-anchor or deadline semantics change.
identity.revision_id: design rev4: derived from (observation, content_hash, gating timestamps)
identity.rss_guid_role: OFFICIAL DISCOVERY IDENTIFIER AND PROVENANCE ONLY - not business identity, not revision identity, not proof of unchanged content
identity.source_item_id: SHA-256 using canonical_serialization over the ordered JSON array [provider_id, event_family, canonical_primary_statement_url], containing exactly those three string values in that order. No other field participates in the logical item hash or identity dedupe.
identity.source_observation_id: design rev4: derived from (provider, source_item_id, content_hash); NEVER URL alone
identity.uniqueness_claim: NOT contractually documented by the provider; identity quality remains GOOD, not EXCELLENT

invariants.F01: Only official allowlisted Federal Reserve surfaces may contribute.
invariants.F02: RSS is discovery, never source-time authority.
invariants.F03: The primary statement page is the semantic authority.
invariants.F04: declared_release_at requires a strict explicit date PLUS an explicit EST/EDT release grammar; it is NEVER a content visibility gate.
invariants.F06: observed_at is the real primary-statement acquisition instant.
invariants.F08: Raw is made durable before any parse.
invariants.F09: Same logical item with changed bytes appends a new immutable revision. For the same provider_id, event_family and canonical_primary_statement_url, mutable content metadata corrections, including official_statement_date, MUST preserve source_item_id; the prior revision remains intact.
invariants.F10: Same bytes create no duplicate revision.
invariants.F11: Last Update never advances original source availability.
invariants.F12: The provider numeric rate limit remains UNKNOWN; the client ceiling is HyprL policy only.
invariants.F13: Raw redistribution is disabled in V1.
invariants.F14: Unknown upstream correction semantics never imply immutability.
invariants.F16: No market, outcome, consensus or LLM field exists in the capture layer.
invariants.F17: The CaptureSpec hash is bound into every normalized revision.
invariants.F19: RELEASE TIME IS NOT CONTENT-VINTAGE PROOF. A provider-declared logical release timestamp must never be used as the source availability of a captured content revision unless the provider contract proves that exact revision became available at that timestamp. For FOMC V1 no such revision-specific proof exists.
invariants.F20: BACKFILL CONTENT VINTAGE. Historical backfill content is visible only from its actual observed/durable timeline unless exact vintage provenance exists. An original release timestamp may describe event metadata but cannot retroactively date the fetched body.
invariants.F21: REVISION-SPECIFIC AVAILABILITY. A later observed content revision cannot inherit an earlier logical event release timestamp as its own source availability. Each revision requires its own availability evidence; absent provider evidence, source_available_at = null.
invariants.F22: ABSENCE CLAIM CANNOT EXCEED CLASSIFIER COVERAGE. An absence assertion must never cover a semantic family broader than the frozen classifier's proven coverage. Where classifier completeness is not established, zero is scoped to the capture predicate only.
invariants.F23: UNRESOLVED CANDIDATE BLOCKS ZERO. Any discovery item that cannot be deterministically classified as IN_SCOPE_V1 or DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE blocks EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO for that check. No exception.
invariants.F24: DISCOVERY/PRIMARY CLASSIFICATION CONFLICT FAILS CLOSED. If discovery metadata indicates an in-scope candidate but the primary page does not satisfy the frozen predicate: no event, no zero, and no silent downgrade to out-of-scope. Diagnostic and raw provenance are recorded under existing source-health semantics.
invariants.F25: MUTABLE CONTENT METADATA MUST NOT DEFINE LOGICAL IDENTITY. Mutable statement metadata parsed from primary-page content, including official_statement_date, MUST NOT participate in source_item_id, the logical item hash or identity dedupe. With provider_id and event_family fixed and the same frozen canonical_primary_statement_url, date corrections preserve the logical item, with or without RSS GUID. Changed bytes append revisions; identical verified bytes under the same CaptureSpec hash must yield the same date, otherwise FAIL CLOSED with no new content revision and no overwrite.
invariants.F26: DISCOVERY URL ANCHORS LOGICAL IDENTITY. For FOMC V1, canonical_primary_statement_url is the official statement link parsed from durable official discovery provenance BEFORE primary redirects, validated and normalized under existing V1 rules. Redirect destinations, final response URLs and HTML canonical URLs are non-identifying provenance and MUST NOT replace this identity input. The rule applies to LIVE feed and HISTORICAL_BACKFILL calendar/archive discovery, with or without RSS GUID. The admitted HTTPS scheme MUST be serialized as exactly lowercase ASCII https in the identity URL; original scheme spelling MUST NOT be hashed as the scheme component of canonical_primary_statement_url.
invariants.F27: TRANSPORT REDIRECTION MUST NOT REKEY AN ITEM. With provider_id, event_family and the normalized official discovery URL fixed, U1 -> U2 and later U1 -> U3 MUST produce the same source_item_id from normalize(U1). Transport movement alone cannot split logical history, cause an identity conflict or create a content revision; changed bytes append revisions under the same item, and unchanged bytes do not duplicate revisions.
invariants.F28: HTTPS SCHEME CASE CANNOT ALTER LOGICAL IDENTITY. HTTPS scheme admission is ASCII case-insensitive; the canonical identity scheme is always exactly lowercase ASCII https. With provider_id, event_family and every other URL component unchanged, changing only upstream HTTPS scheme case MUST preserve canonical_primary_statement_url and source_item_id and MUST NOT create an identity conflict or content revision. Non-HTTPS and empty/missing schemes are rejected, never silently upgraded. Original source spelling is raw discovery provenance only.

classification_states.DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE: the item is excluded by a frozen deterministic negative rule that requires NO semantic guessing. V1 keeps this category deliberately NARROW.
classification_states.IN_SCOPE_V1: the exact frozen positive predicate succeeds on BOTH surfaces
classification_states.UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE: the item appears on the official monetary-policy discovery surface, does not satisfy the positive V1 predicate, and cannot be proven outside the broader monetary/FOMC domain without semantic guessing

item_predicate.default_rationale: fail closed. Unknown relevance resolves to UNRESOLVED, never to a negative. There is no frozen safe negative rule for a differently-titled official monetary item, so the default applies.
item_predicate.evidence: title verified on the four FOMC statement feed items and on statement pages sampled 2015-2026
item_predicate.known_v1_narrowness: an unscheduled or differently-titled FOMC action is NOT captured by V1. It is recorded as an UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE and blocks the zero assertion, rather than being silently treated as absent. Widening the positive predicate requires a spec revision.
item_predicate.no_broad_semantic_classifier: V1 must NOT be widened with keyword lists, semantic similarity, an LLM, regex over body text, or hardcoded emergency-action vocabulary. Honest incompleteness beats speculative coverage.
item_predicate.normalization: exact match after Unicode NFC, HTML entity unescaping, and collapsing runs of ASCII whitespace to one space; comparison is case-sensitive
item_predicate.on_positive_predicate_no_match: classification = UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE unless an explicit frozen negative rule proves DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE. No normalized FOMC EventRevision is created either way, but an UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE BLOCKS any zero assertion for that cycle until it is deterministically resolved.
item_predicate.role: POSITIVE CLASSIFIER FOR THE V1 SUBSET ONLY - a non-match is NOT proof that an item is not an FOMC monetary-policy event
item_predicate.rule: CONJUNCTION - both must hold, on verified official fields only
item_predicate.superseded_rule: rev2 said a non-match was "NOT an FOMC event" - a definitive negative that allowed a false zero. Withdrawn in rev3.

HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.logical_release_metadata: SUPPORTED when the strict parser succeeds

LIVE.logical_release_metadata: SUPPORTED when the strict parser succeeds

mode_capabilities.no_blanket_flag: there is deliberately no ambiguous "retrospective supported" boolean anywhere in this spec

HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.discovery: official FOMC calendar/archive links; URLs never synthesised from dates
HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.raw_first: the archive/calendar page is itself preserved when its links form the provenance of discovery
HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.relabelling: a backfill item is NEVER relabelled LIVE

modes.reconstruction: observed_at is NEVER reconstructed from source timestamps in either mode

normalized_field_notes.canonical_source_url: the existing normalized field carries canonical_primary_statement_url = the normalized official discovery link BEFORE primary redirects; it is not final_response_url or HTML canonical. No schema rename or expansion.
normalized_field_notes.capture_scope_id: binds the deterministic V1 capture subset so downstream cannot confuse provider family with coverage completeness
normalized_field_notes.classification_state: IN_SCOPE_V1 for any admitted revision; the other states never produce a revision
normalized_field_notes.declared_release_at: provider release metadata; NEVER a revision visibility gate
normalized_field_notes.official_statement_date: required normalized metadata of the observed content revision, NEVER logical identity. Date authority and validation remain timestamps.source_date; a date parse failure follows the existing parser/source-health policy. Removing the identity role does not make the date optional.
normalized_field_notes.source_item_id: stable logical identity from provider_id, event_family and the current canonical_primary_statement_url only; official_statement_date is separate revision metadata

parser_policy.determinism: operates offline on locally stored raw bytes only
parser_policy.identity_url_input: supplied by identity.identity_url_authority from durable official discovery provenance; never parsed from primary HTML as a semantic anchor. HTML canonical handling is identity.html_canonical_role.
parser_policy.llm: FORBIDDEN anywhere in ingestion - an LLM may not decide whether something is an FOMC statement, nor its date, release time, identity, revision or source authority

official_statement_date_determinism.failure: PARSER/NORMALIZER DETERMINISM FAILURE is a diagnostic, not a new global source-health state. FAIL CLOSED for parser/spec inconsistency or corruption: no second content revision, no silent normalized mutation; existing raw and immutable revisions remain intact.
official_statement_date_determinism.rule: identical verified persisted primary raw body bytes under the SAME CaptureSpec hash MUST yield identical official_statement_date metadata. A differing date with the same verified body hash is not an upstream content revision.

xml.unsupported_extensions: ignored unless frozen by a spec revision
xml.xxe_note: XML external entity expansion and network entity resolution are a security requirement, not an optimisation

polling.honesty_note: This ceiling is a HyprL client policy. The Federal Reserve has NOT granted a quota of 6 requests/minute or any other figure. Never state or imply otherwise.

retry_policy.rule: on failure, record source health and retry only on the next normal discovery cycle or a scheduled pending-item retry, all under the same ceiling

provider.cadence_note: the EVENT family is a scheduled release, but the COLLECTOR is a plain periodic poll. V1 derives no schedule from FOMC calendars, the 2:00 p.m. tradition, or RSS pubDate.
provider.expected_latency: UNKNOWN - feed cadence undocumented; bounded in practice by the client poll interval
provider.historical_availability: statement pages retrievable by official archive link; explicit release line verified on samples across 2016-2026
provider.official_contract: no published numeric rate limit; no verified prohibition of automated access
provider.revision_support: UPSTREAM UNKNOWN - handled client-side by content-hash re-observation, never by assuming immutability
provider.taxonomy_note: existing frozen rev4 value reused; NO new taxonomy introduced
provider.timestamp_quality: EXCELLENT for the LOGICAL RELEASE DECLARATION when the strict grammar matches. NOT a content-revision availability timestamp: no revision-specific source availability is exposed by the contract.

raw_policy.bytes_semantics: raw_body_bytes = the entity body AFTER standard HTTP content decoding; Content-Encoding retained as metadata
raw_policy.charset: determined only AFTER the raw artefact exists; invalid or unexpected encoding => PARSER_FAILED; no lossy decode before hashing
raw_policy.hash_algorithm_note: repo primitive sha256_bytes; no second digest algorithm introduced
raw_policy.hash_is_not_vintage_proof: the raw body hash is provenance for WHAT HYPRL ACTUALLY OBSERVED AND WHEN. It does not become proof of historical content existence merely because the same normalized record also carries a declared_release_at recovered from the page.
raw_policy.parser_precondition: a parser never consumes bytes not already represented by a durable raw identity
raw_policy.pdf_note: a PDF of each statement exists but V1 is HTML-only; adding it requires a spec revision

redistribution.release_guard: existing repo release policy applies unchanged
redistribution.why_stricter_than_evidence: the Federal Reserve disclaimer states that, unless otherwise indicated, Board website information is in the public domain. V1 is nonetheless stricter: 6G-A does not need redistribution, and a blanket DISABLED avoids per-item 'unless otherwise indicated' rights analysis and keeps the release guard simple.

retrospective_source_fit.metadata_only_layer: a distinct metadata-only release-fact layer may be useful later, but it would need its own schema and design. This CaptureSpec does NOT invent one.
never_claims: that HyprL observed the statement historically
that the fetched bytes were the bytes visible at declared_release_at
retrospective_source_fit.retrospective_release_time_metadata: SUPPORTED - declared_release_at may be recorded as non-gating provenance
retrospective_source_fit.rule: A content-bearing revision with observation_mode = HISTORICAL_BACKFILL is NOT eligible to become source-visible at declared_release_at. It is visible only on its actual observed/durable timeline.
retrospective_source_fit.trust_policy_cannot_override: no TimestampTrustPolicyV1 verdict may substitute for missing content-vintage proof. A TRUSTED_EXACT release timestamp means "the source reliably declares the logical release at T" - it does NOT mean "every currently fetched byte existed at T".
retrospective_source_fit.validated_scope_note: explicit EST/EDT release lines were verified on SAMPLES across 2016-2026, and a "For immediate release" counterexample at 2015-03-18. V1 claims NO universal coverage. The parser is RECORD-SPECIFIC.
retrospective_source_fit.why: the historical vintage of the exact page body is not established by the verified provider contract

revision_note: Spec revision 6 addresses the MEDIUM found at point 8 of counter-review R5: HTTPS scheme output casing was unspecified in the identity-bearing normalized URL. Scheme admission is now explicitly ASCII case-insensitive HTTPS only, and canonical identity serialization always emits lowercase ASCII https. Other or empty/missing schemes are rejected without upgrade. Original spelling remains raw discovery provenance. F26 is strengthened; F28 and FOMC31/FOMC32 bind the fix. FIX1-FIX4 are preserved, including the official discovery URL authority before redirects. Every non-scheme URL rule, raw policy, scheduler and timeout remains unchanged. No design change, runtime or safe_http edit, fixture, network or independent counter-review in this fix; full review remains pending.

revision_policy.overwrite: FORBIDDEN - neither raw nor normalized revisions are ever overwritten
revision_policy.post_window_limitation: V1 makes NO promise to detect upstream changes after +7 days. This is an explicit, stated limitation, not an immutability claim. Extending the schedule requires CaptureSpec V2.
revision_policy.reobservation_anchor: the first successful primary statement fetch
revision_policy.reobservation_rationale: detects immediate, same-day, next-day and delayed corrections; ~4 extra requests per statement at roughly 8 statements a year is negligible
revision_policy.same_item_same_body_hash: same content revision; NO duplicate revision created
revision_policy.unchanged_refetch: still raw-first with auditable observation metadata; no duplicate normalized revision

scope.broad_domain: Federal Reserve monetary-policy press-release content (the discovery surface)
explicitly_out_of_scope: all other Federal Reserve press releases
scope.honest_statement: This provider V1 does NOT claim to cover every possible FOMC action or communication. It positively classifies exactly one release pattern, and every absence claim it makes is scoped to that pattern.
in_scope: FOMC monetary-policy statements published as official Federal Reserve press releases AND matching the frozen positive predicate
scope.taxonomy_note: the frozen rev4 taxonomy type is retained; capture_scope_id records that V1 captures a deterministic SUB-FAMILY of it
scope.v1_target_subset: official items satisfying the frozen positive FOMC-statement predicate
scope.why_narrow: first EventStore proof; one event family, deterministic, causally honest, offline-replayable

security_requirements: redirect destinations validated before being followed
no cookies as a correctness dependency

mappings.release line is 'For immediate release': NOT a health failure - event valid, source_available_at unavailable

source_health.never: a network failure is missingness, NEVER evidence of zero events. And an absence claim requires MORE than retrieval and parsing: it requires COMPLETE deterministic classification of every relevant item with zero unresolved candidates. Fetch + parse success alone is NOT sufficient to assert absence.
source_health.scope_note: a feed outage must NOT mark all Federal Reserve data globally unavailable
source_health.state_reuse_note: UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE and classification conflict map onto the existing rev4 PARSER_FAILED state: classification is a normalization step over fetched bytes, and rev4 constrains PARSER_FAILED by name only. No sixth global state is invented. The provider-local classification outcome is carried as a diagnostic detail attached to that frozen state.
source_health.vocabulary: design rev4 missingness_policy states only; no new global state invented

status_meaning: Semantics are frozen. NOT implemented, NOT captured, NOT live. Any runtime implementation must conform exactly or require a spec revision.
structured_economic_extraction: DEFERRED - not required to identify the statement family; belongs to a later enrichment phase

surfaces.allowlist_note: exact host only. The apex federalreserve.gov is NOT allowlisted: no canonical redirect requirement was verified for it. No wildcard. HTTPS only, port 443 only, no userinfo.

discovery.role: LIVE DISCOVERY ONLY - never source-time authority

primary.path_constraint_role: VALIDATION of an officially supplied link, never a construction rule
primary.role: PRIMARY SEMANTIC AUTHORITY - source content, date and release instant
primary.url_source: MUST come from an official discovery link (live feed item <link>, or an official FOMC calendar/archive link in backfill). URLs are NEVER constructed from a date.

content_source_available_at.consequence: revision availability is bounded by observed_at and commit-bound ingested_at, and is revision-specific
content_source_available_at.design_compatibility: design rev4 already supports a null source_available_at bounded by observed_at; NO new design primitive is introduced
content_source_available_at.lifted_only_by: a future CaptureSpec version carrying a VERIFIED revision-specific source availability timestamp
content_source_available_at.rule: EVERY content-bearing EventRevision produced by this CaptureSpec has source_available_at = null, in BOTH observation modes, with NO exception - including the first live body, and including a body whose page prints an exact release line.
content_source_available_at.why: The Federal Reserve contract verified in provider rev3 exposes NO revision-specific source availability timestamp. The release line dates the LOGICAL EVENT, not the byte sequence HyprL holds. Assigning it to a content revision would retroproject a possibly-later body to the original release instant.

declared_release_at.null_when: the release line is "For immediate release", or no accepted grammar matches
declared_release_at.role: PROVIDER-DECLARED RELEASE TIME FOR THE LOGICAL EVENT - NON-GATING PROVENANCE ONLY
stored_alongside: timestamp_trust_verdict for the RELEASE CLAIM only
declared_release_at.what_it_does_NOT_establish: that the currently observed body bytes existed, or were public, at that instant
declared_release_at.what_it_establishes: that the source declares the logical FOMC statement released at this instant

http_last_modified.lifted_only_by: a provider-specific verified semantic contract, which V1 does not have

immediate_release.not_parser_failed: this is a recognised syntax, NOT a parse failure; the event is not corrupted merely because no clock exists
immediate_release.timestamp_semantics: UNKNOWN (existing TimestampTrustPolicyV1 vocabulary; no new design vocabulary introduced)
immediate_release.verdict: VALID PAGE, VALID EVENT. No declared exact release time, and - as for every other FOMC revision in V1 - no content source availability either.

ingested_at.definition: inherited unchanged from design rev4: the successful authoritative normalized EventStore commit boundary
ingested_at.lost_ack: the existing committed revision remains authoritative and is rediscovered idempotently

last_update.no_derived_timestamp: no normalized causal timestamp may be derived from it
last_update.permitted_use: optional non-causal diagnostic; if stored at all, retain only the literal display text as provenance

observed_at.definition: the instant the collector successfully receives the PRIMARY statement raw bytes used for that revision
observed_at.historical_backfill: the actual backfill collection instant; NEVER reconstructed

release_time.bare_ET: NOT ACCEPTED in V1 - no timezone guess; source_available_at unavailable
release_time.evidence: EST verified on 2025-12-10, 2026-01-28 and 2019-01-30; EDT verified across 2016-2026 samples
release_time.normalization: HTML entities unescaped; runs of ASCII whitespace collapsed to one space; leading/trailing whitespace stripped; match is otherwise literal and case-sensitive
release_time.role_in_v1: NON-GATING provider-declared release metadata. The strict grammar is RETAINED unchanged; only its role changed - it no longer gates content revision visibility.
release_time.timezone_inference: FORBIDDEN - the abbreviation is read from the document, never derived from the date

rss_pubdate.on_disagreement_with_primary: record a diagnostic; NEVER silently rewrite the primary timestamp
rss_pubdate.use_as_content_revision_availability: FORBIDDEN - even when it equals the declared release time
rss_pubdate.why: semantics are not officially documented, and a GMT value alone is ambiguous with respect to local release semantics - 19:00Z is both 2:00 p.m. EST and 3:00 p.m. EDT

source_date.accepted_grammar: US long form '<Month> <D>, <YYYY>' as printed adjacent to the statement title
source_date.evidence: verified structure: date line, then 'Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement', then the release line

source_updated_at.note: the R1 finding proposed populating this from the page Last Update field. That proposal is REJECTED: provider rev3 established Last Update as page-maintenance metadata, not a verified content-revision publication timestamp. A wrong vintage signal is worse than a declared absent one.
source_updated_at.rule: null for every FOMC content revision in V1
source_updated_at.why: design rev4 offers the field, but no VERIFIED provider signal establishes the public availability time of a specific content revision. Absence recorded honestly rather than filled with a proxy.

unrecognised_release_syntax.distinct_from: immediate_release, which is recognised and valid

url_canonicalization.query: V1 requires queryless canonical statement URLs; a query component is unexpected and fails closed
url_canonicalization.raw_source_scheme_spelling: PROVENANCE_ONLY - original source spelling remains available in the durable raw discovery artifact. Do not rewrite those raw bytes to canonicalize identity. The derived canonical_primary_statement_url always uses lowercase ASCII https, regardless of original scheme spelling.

scheme_admission.comparison_rule: compare the parsed scheme to https after mapping ASCII A-Z to a-z only; no Unicode case folding or scheme inference

scheme_normalization_order: 1. extract the official discovery URL from durable discovery provenance
3. compare the parsed scheme against https ASCII case-insensitively
4. reject if the scheme is not HTTPS, including empty/missing scheme; no source_item_id admission or primary request
5. after successful HTTPS validation, serialize the identity URL scheme as exactly lowercase ASCII https
6. apply all OTHER existing V1 URL normalization rules unchanged; existing non-scheme validation requirements remain mandatory

visibility.declared_release_at_effect: NONE - it never alters content visibility

design_general_form.note: quoted from design rev4 for reference; V1 content revisions only ever use the second form

v1_content_revisions.note: V1 always takes the null branch; the exact-timestamp branch is unreachable for content revisions

blocked_by: a candidate whose primary fetch failed
a candidate whose primary parse failed
zero_assertion.design_alignment: design rev4 missingness_policy.never_encoded_as_zero = true; unresolved classification is not zero
zero_assertion.downstream_restriction: EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO from this provider MUST NOT be interpreted downstream as "the Federal Reserve/FOMC produced no monetary-policy event". No model or feature may treat it as a complete-world event count unless a future coverage contract establishes completeness. This binds later InformationSnapshot composition.
zero_assertion.forbidden_wording: never state "zero FOMC events" or equivalent without the capture-scope qualifier. This is a CAPTURE-SCOPE absence assertion, not a world-state one.
preconditions_all_required: 2. the raw feed artefact was durably persisted
4. every feed item relevant to this capture scope was classified deterministically
6. no primary-page fetch or parse remains unresolved for a candidate that could affect the V1 result
7. the number of newly admitted IN_SCOPE_V1 events = 0
zero_assertion.semantic_scope: ZERO CONFIRMED V1-SUBSET EVENTS. Precisely: "no new events matching federal_reserve_fomc_capture_v1's frozen V1 predicate were confirmed during this successful discovery cycle."
